verdict: No production defect or unsupported completion/compatibility claim identified in the reviewed Split diff and current contract.
scope: Dedicated static/runtime direct-assignment cases; Split name reservation; unaffected ordinary scalar/element/property assignment paths
Strict local dynamic String-array admission and recursive static checking of inactive source and unused procedures
Old descriptor reads and once-only, left-to-right argument evaluation; lock precedence; publish-after-validation/storage construction
Exact nonoverlapping UTF-16 matching, positive-limit suffix preservation, empty input and zero limit
Per-array and active-slot limits; stored String unit accounting; work charging for matching/allocation/retirement/copying
Allocated empty bounds, Join/For Each/indexing, Erase and ReDim Preserve interoperability
Caller versus helper frame ownership, local resource release, shared global work accounting
Corpus independence, native/CLI/MCP test assertions and portable output claims
Public contract distinctions between implemented dialect behavior and installed Office compatibility
observations: Result count is checked before List allocation; positive caps preserve the full remaining suffix. stringUnits equals source UTF-16 length less only matched delimiters, including capped results.
Replacement computes available capacity with old slot/String occupancy credited, charges retirement and new copy work before allocating, then updates counters and descriptor together.
For Each uses descriptor identity and finally/Exit cleanup; Split refuses a locked descriptor before invoking argument helpers. Empty descriptors are allocated with bounds 0..-1 and length 0.
Helpers cannot alias caller arrays under the existing parameter rules. Active caller counts stay charged during helper execution and are restored on return; global work is never reset.

The change does not modify native operations or document admission. Word integration and CLI tests verify atomic failures and inert payload preservation; they do not claim signature validity or embedded VBA execution.
The corpus has 58 independently authored cases, adapted to three fixed output sinks without deriving expected results from the compiler. Provenance separates spec-derived and dialect-contract cases.

Microsoft primary reference confirms zero-based results, default space, empty-input array, empty-delimiter behavior and -1 for all substrings. MS-VBAL has the documented 1/-1 inconsistency. Named/omitted arguments, general array values, coercion/locale modes and Office-host qualification remain explicitly excluded.

No broad test suite was rerun for this review. Earlier agent development acceptance was 9/9 new integration/CLI cases, clean scoped analysis, and parsed-equivalent actual-BAS VM/JS receipts; root final gate remains responsible for final integrated-source acceptance.
